column2: Come on, let's hurry and go look for it!”
{n2} and I passed through the basement door and descended into the labyrinth from which, they say, no one has ever returned alive.
Going down the stairs, a cold blast hit us.
It was a clammy, unpleasant chill.
maybe we should go back after all.”
This is only the first floo-”
Just as I started to say that.
A creature that, just by looking, could be nothing but a goblin, so goblin-y and so gob-lean.
So that's a goblin's cry... but this was no time to be impressed.
a mosquito could land on that.{r}{p}This is how you throw a real punch!”
The goblin burned out to pure white ash.
The goblin had money.{r}{p}Look, he's even got a coin purse... all small change.{r}{p}Maybe he picked it up from under vending machines.{r}{p}Pitiful.{r}{p}Let's see...
Having gotten the money, we moved on.
“Well, there's this guy named Jean-Claude Van Damme, you know...
“Then I'll go with this one instead.{r}{p}There may be copyright issues, but who cares...
For some reason that exact spot was rocky ground.
The goblin fell, and the next instant exploded
“Hey, a UFO!” I said, pointing behind it.
{n2} leaned forward and looked into the distance alongside the goblin.
Why are you falling for it, {n2}?!”
Realizing it had been tricked, the goblin lunged at me, breathing stinking breath.
The goblin's knobby fingers wrapped firmly around my throat.
The instant I heard {n2}'s voice, the fingers loosened.
I grabbed the goblin's arm and twisted it up.
“Well yeah, for the sake of the story.”
...So that's that. Please help me out.”
I can't help you for free.”
“If you tell me where the Box of Happiness is, I'll let you go.”
I'll tell you, so please let go of my arm!”
The goblin said, rubbing his arm.
And with that the goblin ran off at top speed.
Down below? Tell me which floor, you rascal!”
It's probably somewhere around basement level 27.”
“Woman's intuition, woman's intuition.{r}{p}Come on, let's move on.”
“If you give me ten thousand yen, I might consider it.”
The goblin scratched his head and chuckled.
“Even so, the recession has hit this industry hard, too.”
The goblin said, wiping the sweat off his forehead with a handkerchief he took out from somewhere.
even the monster industry is in a slump...”
I'll let you off for 180 yen.”
you'd better stay away from the spring on basement level 5.{r}{p}You'll definitely regret it.{r}{p}Consider it a thank-you; please remember it.”
Better not go near the spring.{r}{p}Should I write that down?”
“We can remember that much, can't we?”
We'd be fools if we couldn't remember something that simple.”
I laughed weakly, with a trace of unease.
As we advanced, we found a staircase leading down.
I looked where {n2} was pointing and saw a neon arrow glowing.
No reason not to use modern conveniences.”
{n2} agreed, which emboldened me, and I got into the elevator.
There were only buttons for B1 and B5.
The elevator descended smoothly to basement level 5 and the doors opened.
A dazzling flood of neon hit us.
Neon of every color filled the labyrinth, pointing the way with arrows.
“'Fountain' is English for a spring, isn't it?”
'Fountain' obviously sounds like 'mountain,' so it means mountain.”
We followed the neon guidance through the labyrinth.
Soon we came out into a slightly open area, with a round spring with a peeing-boy statue in the center.
Oh no, we went near the spring we were told to avoid!”
I remembered the goblin's warning and panicked.
{n2} and I hurriedly tried to run.
An iron grate came clanging down in front of us, trapping us inside.
I looked around, but there was no exit in sight.
I tried to recall the goblin's words.
I think he'd said, 'You'll definitely regret it.'
Did that mean we'd be locked in and never get out?
Or was something even more terrible going to happen...?
“There must be some way to escape.”
{n2} said encouragingly, so I decided to examine the area around the spring.
Though it was called a spring, there wasn't a single drop of water in it; it was bone dry.
On the stone in front, this was carved.
'Drink holy water from the holy chalice.
Then the way shall be opened.'
“Holy chalice?{r}{p} Where's that supposed to be?”
I didn't have an item like that.
Is a reset the only option...
{n2} pointed at the peeing-boy statue in the center.
Looking closely, an enameled cup sat on the statue's pedestal.
“It looks like a bathroom cup, but...
since there's nothing else, I guess we have to assume that's it.{r}{p}...But where's the water?”
We climbed over the stonework and approached the peeing boy.
“This is no time to be shy.{r}{p}Look for something like a main valve that makes the water come out.”
As I said that, I picked up the cup and casually held it out where the peeing boy's water should come out.
The instant I did, water gushed into the cup.
Drank the water in the cup in one gulp.
And suddenly, the statue began to move!
Ahh, I'm tired.{r}{p}All right, all right,
you drank the 'holy water' properly, I see.{r}{p}I'll let you out now, so wait there.”
With that, the peeing boy stepped down from the pedestal, went to the wall, opened a hidden door, and operated something.
The iron grating began to rise slowly.
“Come back anytime you feel like it.”
With that, the peeing boy chuckled and climbed back onto the pedestal.
{n2} patted my shoulder as I stood there in a daze.
“Well, just think of it as being bitten by a stray dog and forget about it quickly.”
Coming to my senses, I ran to the wall and tried to throw up by sticking my fingers down my throat.
Nothing came out but stomach acid.
Tears came from the agony and humiliation.
Half dragged along by {n2}, I returned to the elevator, went back to basement level 1, and took the stairs down to level 2.
We took the elevator back up to basement level 1 and took the stairs down to level 2.
A sign like that could be a trap.”
Let's take the stairs for now.”
I thought how lucky I was to finally see the long-awaited Nessie in a place like this.
Why are you falling for it, {n1}?!”
Even if there were a dinosaur here, you couldn't call it Nessie!
By the time I realized it, it was too late, and the goblin's sharp claws were already sunk into my throat.
{n2} asked back, but no words came out of my mouth anymore.
As my consciousness faded, I thought.
If there were a dinosaur here, what would its name be?
That was the last word that came to my mind.
It might be the most pathetic death in the history of video games.
“If you give me a strong weapon or something, I'll help you.”
The goblin took off the backpack he was carrying and began rummaging through it.
An iron ball was attached by chain to the end of a stick.
It resembled a weapon you see a lot in RPGs.
Spikes are dangerous, so I improved it myself.{r}{p}I call it the Morning Moon.”
What's the point of making it weaker?{p}Don't you have a stronger one?”
...How about this?{r}{p}A sword with a magic effect.”
“I added a sleep effect to a falchion.{r}{p}I call it the Halcion {C3}(a sleeping pill){C0}.{r}{p}It sometimes causes hallucinations too.”
It saps my will to fight.{r}{p}Don't you have something cooler?
Like a Dragon Killer or an orichalcum sword.”
“Well, unfortunately this is about all I've got...”
Just then I caught sight of another sword-like thing in the backpack.
“What are you talking about? Show me.”
I knocked the goblin's arm aside and pulled the sword out of the backpack.
A piece of paper was stuck on the scabbard, reading “Muramasa” {C3}(legendary cursed katana){C0}.
look at this nice thing you've got.{r}{p}I'll take it.”
“It's not about being stingy.{r}{p}Something terrible happens if you draw it.”
Well, I'll believe you.{r}{p}Then I'll make do with this Halcion sword.”
The goblin left, wiping the sweat from his forehead.
“He seemed really relieved.{r}{p}Do you think something terrible really would have happened?”
Moving ahead, we found a staircase leading down.
This is where it really begins.”
Basement level 2 was dim and had poor visibility.
The moment I muttered that, the area lit up.
At {n2}'s shout I whirled around, and a huge figure wrapped in flames stood blocking the way!
Isn't that a bit too scary for the second floor?{r}{p}Slugs or mushrooms are normal, right?”
No amount of crying or yelling about game balance did any good.
“Maybe it's actually weak if you fight it!{r}{p}You got a sword earlier, too!”
{n2} gave advice from about thirty feet away, having somehow run off already.
Feel the power of the goblin's special Halcion!”
I slammed the magic sword Halcion into the flame demon.
The instant the sword's tip reached the demon, drowsiness hit... me.
He'd only said “added a sleep effect”; he never said it would put the enemy to sleep.
Just before I crumpled and fell asleep, I felt my whole body engulfed in flames.
I was sure he was lying.
“It's no good saying that.{r}{p}If it's Muramasa, it's the best weapon in games, that's a given.”
The goblin wouldn't let go of the Muramasa, and it turned into a tug-of-war.
Are you going to defy Robert Woodhead {C3}(creator of Wizardry){C0}, the god of RPGs?{p}Just hand it over!”
I finally wrested the Muramasa from the goblin's hand, drew the sword from its scabbard, and gazed at the blade.
It was a beautiful blade without a single blemish.
A shiver ran down my spine.
Looking up, I saw the goblin staring at me and starting to back away.
I'm not done with you yet.”
The goblin let out a very un-monsterlike scream, turned his back, and bolted.
I leaped after him and swung the Muramasa down on the goblin's back.
Its back split in two, green body fluid shot up to the ceiling and spattered everywhere.
The greatest rush of pleasure I'd ever known ran through my whole body.
Even an amateur like me could cut a monster clean in half, so the sharpness was incredible.
Turning around, I saw {n2}, splattered with green, sitting on the floor trembling.
With this Muramasa, we can wipe out every monster.”
Aren't you the one acting weird?”
What was she saying, throw away this greatest of swords?
There's no way I'd throw it away.”
“...Then I'm going outside.{r}{p}I can't stand to look at you like this.”
If you've gotten sick of me, I won't force you.”
Suddenly my arm began to itch.
It felt like something was flowing in from the palm gripping the Muramasa.
A voiceless thought flowed into me from the Muramasa.
{n2} shook her head as if begging.
Without realizing it, I had raised the Muramasa overhead.
...When I came to, I was standing at the bottom of the basement stairs, covered in red and green splatters.
I couldn't remember when I'd left the dungeon.
Suddenly I wondered what had become of {n2}.
We'd been together just a moment ago.
I had a feeling something fun had happened, but I couldn't remember it.
Shaking my head, I climbed the stairs.
When I opened the door and went out, Mr. Kobayashi was there and cried out in astonishment at the sight of me.
He noticed the Muramasa and fell silent.
The Muramasa flashed once, and Mr. Kobayashi's head rolled on the floor.
A cry of joy echoed through the inn.
It was the joyful cry of both the sword and me.
Turning, I saw Kyoko standing in front of the dining room.
I covered those several yards in an instant,
and slashed her side as I passed.
The voice of joy that had been flowing in all this time and the cry for blood could no longer be heard.
I stopped being the wind and stood still.
The hilt that had seemed glued to my palm came away for no reason, and the Muramasa fell to the floor, standing at a slant.
Everything since I'd picked up the Muramasa replayed in my head.
I'd killed the goblin, killed {n2}, killed Mr. Kobayashi, Kyoko, Mr. Kayama, Mr. Mikimoto, Midori...!
Hadn't I been having a bad dream?
Looking through an open door, I saw three girls inside, dead like scraps of rags.
I looked away and ran down the stairs.
What looked like Mr. Kobayashi's headless body and Kyoko lay fallen.
That sword had turned me into a murderous maniac.
And since there was no one left here to kill, it had left my hand...
I fell to my knees and collapsed on the floor.
If this is a dream, I want to wake up soon.
Then I noticed the Muramasa, which I should have left upstairs, lying beside me.
The blade, which should have been bloody a moment ago, shone without a single cloud, as it had when I first drew it.
As if bewitched, I reached out.
I stood it hilt-down on the floor and put the point to my throat.
If it's a dream, I'll wake up.
Shutting my eyes tight, I leaned my weight forward.
For some reason I didn't feel like drinking it.
peered into the cup of water.
It was somehow yellowish and had a pungent smell.
Even if it's a little dirty, we can't get out unless you drink it!”
could you drink it for me?”
A girl's body is delicate.{r}{p}You drink it, {n1}.”
True, I couldn't make {n2} drink something like this.
Going further, we found another staircase leading down.
I nodded to {n2} and quietly descended.
Basement level 2 was dim and had poor visibility.
The moment I muttered that, the area lit up.
At {n2}'s shout I whirled around, and a huge figure wrapped in flames stood blocking the way!
wait a second!{r}{p}Isn't that a bit too scary for the second floor?{r}{p}Slugs or mushrooms are normal, right?”
No amount of crying or yelling about game balance did any good.
thought it might actually be weak and leaped at it.
Flames stretched out like tongues and clung to my whole body.
I could tell my hair was burning, then my clothes, and then my flesh blistering.
I rolled on the floor trying to put out the fire, but my consciousness faded fast...
I decided to run, and quickly.
With no weapon or anything, I couldn't take on a guy like this.
Being so big, the flame demon moved slowly, and escaping was easy.
When the flame demon was out of sight, we came to a fork.
The right path was dark and gave off a smell like a sewer.
The left path was brighter and drier than the right.
As we went down the left path, it gradually got brighter.
Starting to miss fresh air, I voiced some wishful thinking.
Light seemed to be shining in from around it.
I hurried a bit to the corner and turned it.
Right then, I ran into a flame demon.
So this guy was why it was bright!”
I tried to retreat, but the earlier demon was coming from behind.
{n2} and I were roasted golden brown, like saury in a grill.
Walking down the right path, we soon came to a staircase leading down.
the flame demon was chasing us!
I didn't need {n2} to tell me; I was already running down the stairs.
Where the stairs ended was a large square room.
Turning and looking up, the flame demon peered down with a resentful look.
Catching my breath, I looked around the room.
Each of the four walls had three wooden doors.
“There are twelve in total!{r}{p}Which way are we supposed to go?”
“We'll just check them one by one.”
As I looked around wondering where to start, a voice came down from the sky.
{n2} said, looking around for whoever was there.
I'm obviously talking about you two!”
was that it.{r}{p}...By the way, who are you to call people you've just met fools?”
You'll find out in due time.{r}{p}If you manage to reach me alive.”
“And now, it's time for 'The Twelve Doors'!{r}{p}Only one door is correct.
All the others hold instant death, no mercy.{r}{p}Now, open the correct door!”
Wondering what kind of death I'd meet, I looked over the room again.
Each door had a symbol or number carved into it.
“What are these numbers?{r}{p}What do they mean?”
I forgot to give you a hint.{r}{p}Listen up.
Open the door below the 4.{r}{p}Below the 4,
What's that supposed to mean?{r}{p}I don't get it!”
I complained, but the voice no longer made a peep.
I'm surviving this no matter what.”
With eyes wide open, I examined the fronts of the twelve doors.
stopped in front of the north wall.
Three doors marked 4, 2, and $ stood in a row.
I boldly opened the door marked '4.'
A skeleton in a black cloak stood before me.
The instant I thought something flashed, I was looking up from the ground.
A man stood facing a scythe-wielding Grim Reaper...
and that man had no head!
The moment I realized it, my headless body toppled over.
that blood flowed all the way to where my face was.
even as only a head I'm still conscious...
I boldly opened the door marked '2.'
A giant duck scooped me up in its bill and swallowed me with a gulp.
In its pitch-dark stomach I was tossed about in powerful digestive juices.
With agonizing pain my flesh began to melt away,
and everything was wrapped in the smell of blood and acid...
I boldly opened the door marked '$.'
Before I had time to feel pain, my strength drained fast,
I stopped in front of the east wall.
Three doors marked 6, 9, and 3 stood in a row.
I boldly opened the door marked '6.'
A woman dressed in white sat there.
When she looked up, she smiled sweetly.
Then, all at once, her face turned demonic, and her neck began to stretch out!
I tried to run, but her pale neck coiled around my face.
Before long, my consciousness faded away...
I boldly opened the door marked '9.'
A giant iron ball came rolling out!
With no time to dodge, I was crushed flat under that ball...
I boldly opened the door marked '3.'
The moment I tried to approach,
I stopped in front of the west wall.
Three doors marked 1, *, and 7 stood in a row.
I boldly opened the door marked '1.'
A giant Doberman inside glared at me and barked.
Before I could flee, the Doberman bit into my throat and tore through it like paper.
Watching the bright blood spray out, I lost consciousness...
I boldly opened the door marked '*.'
A huge quantity of packed-in rice came pouring out!
Before I could flee, I was buried in rice.
I heard my chest being crushed by the weight and my ribs breaking.
I boldly opened the door marked '7.'
an invitation to the bottom of the abyss!”
Suddenly the floor tilted, {n2} and I lost our balance and fell, sliding out through the door.
The passage sloped like a slide, and we went down at tremendous speed.
I stopped in front of the south wall.
Three doors marked 5, 0, and 8 stood in a row.
I boldly opened the door marked '5.'
Pitch-black darkness spread beyond the door.
Then the darkness began to invade toward us!
It crawled along the floor to my feet, and then started climbing my body.
A swarm of cockroaches crawled up with a rustling sound, from my feet to my chest to my face.
The instant I tried to brush them off with my hand, I felt a stinging pain.
They covered my face, crept into my clothes, and began to chew through my skin.
With my vision blotted out in black,
bleeding from all over, I collapsed...
I boldly opened the door marked '0.'
There was nothing beyond the door.
It was an infinite space with not even air.
The air in the room rushed out with a roar, and {n2} and I were thrown out together.
Floating in the void, spinning round and round, my consciousness faded...
I boldly opened the door marked '8.'
Something came sliding out and coiled around my body.
Two, three thick, slimy tentacles squeezed me.
My ribs creaked and cracked and agonizing pain shot through me.
A clot of blood welled from my mouth.
From level 3 to level 27?{r}{p}This dungeon is like a fare dodger.”
“Come to think of it, it was a long road...”
I'm saying it's like cheating on a train fare by paying only at the ends...”
“On level 7 we wandered a deadly maze, and on level 12 a wizard caught us and nearly turned us into frogs.”
On level 19 we strayed into a dragon's lair and almost got roasted whole, and on level 21 we had to solve the Sphinx's riddle.”
Now that she mentioned it, I did kind of feel like...
level 25 was awful!{p}Surrounded by a swarm of snakes.”
That didn't happen.{r}{p}Level 25 was surprisingly easy.”
I wasn't convinced, but decided not to argue.
“More importantly, this is the last floor, so there must be even scarier enemies waiting than ever before.{r}{p}Don't let your guard down.”
I swallowed hard and looked around.
A vast open space stretched out, and not a sound could be heard.
“It looks like there's nothing here, though...”
They're lulling us into letting our guard down, planning to attack from somewhere unexpected.”
I laughed and stomped on the stone floor.
A low rumbling sound came, and I felt the floor sway.
The walls and ceiling were undulating along with the floor.
As {n2} said, it wasn't the way an earthquake shakes.
...it's alive!{p}This whole floor is the monster!”
The moment I shouted that, a familiar voice reached us.
You've come this far overcoming countless deadly traps.{r}{p}The death roulette on level 6, the magic circle on level 9, the escape from the nonexistent level 13... {g}
“I keep telling you, we came from level 3 straight to here!”
“More importantly, what does 'not quite right but close' mean?”
“I did say this floor might be the monster, didn't I?{r}{p}That is not quite accurate.{r}{p}You two were inside me from the very beginning.”
With a bad feeling, I timidly asked.
“I am the industry's first labyrinth with a mind of its own.{r}{p}People call me, with fear and respect... 'Mr. Labyrinth.'”
I couldn't help slipping into Kansai dialect {C3}(the Osaka area){C0} as I shot back.
How did you come to have a mind?”
{n2} seemed to be adapting to this bizarre situation right away.
“...That is a difficult question.{r}{p}I doubt you could answer such a thing yourselves,
but we're living things, at least... And you're made of stone and wood, right?”

“There is a hypothesis of sorts.{r}{p}As monsters came and went through the complex maze, they formed a kind of nervous system.{r}{p}You could call it the collective unconscious of monsters.{r}{p}It rebuilt the maze and eventually crystallized into a single will
It sounded like I understood it and didn't.
But since a dungeon was actually talking, I had no choice but to believe it.
“...By the way, if I may ask something off topic, is there a Box of Happiness on this floor?”
“Of course there is.{r}{p}Isn't that what you've been adventuring for?”
Will you give it to us?”
{n2} suddenly perked up and began to beam.{g}
Following the voice, I looked around,
and there was a gold-shining treasure chest... two of them, in fact.
There are two Boxes of Happiness?”
When {n2} said that in wonder, 'Mr. Labyrinth' spoke.{g}
“Naturally, only one is genuine.{r}{p}Choose whichever you like.”
{n2} and I looked at each other, nodded, and slowly approached the two chests.
The two treasure chests were so alike that they were completely indistinguishable.
I glared at the two boxes.

I forgot to mention, the fake one is of course called the 'Box of Unhappiness,' and it's packed with all the misery in the world.{r}{p}If you open it by mistake, terrible things will happen.{r}{p}Your alarm clock won't ring and you'll be late for school,
your guesses for the test will all be wrong...”
“...Depending on the case, your game save data might vanish...”
{n2} and I shouted at the same time.
It means you'd better be ready for that much when you open one.{r}{p}Now, which will it be?”
Since today is a blowout sale, I'll give you a special hint.{r}{p}Listen well and think.”
“...What governs the hand that holds the bow?
“What governs the hand that holds the bow...?”
No more than that.{r}{p}Now, which do you open?{r}{p}The right?{r}{p}
'Mr. Labyrinth' pressed us for a decision.
Which hand do you hold a bow with?{r}{p}The left, I guess...
You nock the arrow with the right...
No, is it the other way around?”
I put my hand on the lid and lifted it with all my strength.
A beautiful melody poured out from inside.
Well done solving my riddle.{r}{p}To know that the left hand is governed by the right brain, I am impressed.”
“The left hand by the right brain...?
I see, so that's what it meant.{r}{p}{n1}, you're pretty sharp.”
I decided to keep quiet about having picked at random.
I closed my eyes and gave myself to the music.
So the Box of Happiness was a music box?
“'Mr. Labyrinth,' you said it's packed with happiness, but is this all?”
“What more could you ask for than this beautiful music?”
“Well, like tasty food, pretty clothes, money... That's what happiness is, isn't it!”
Don't you think you lack romance?”
Can romance fill yer belly?{r}{p}It's money that makes the world go 'round, money.”
“Well, such a view is fine too.{r}{p}If you want a little bonus, dye your bookmark gold.
Then you'll be able to enjoy a slightly naughty{g}
sound drama hidden inside this DISC.”
“You'll have to find that out yourself.{r}{p}It is your last and greatest task.{r}{p}Fwoh ho ho.”
His presence seemed about to vanish.
Just as one especially loud voice echoed, space twisted and warped.
...When I came to, we were standing in front of the basement door.
For a while we stood there dumbfounded, as if we'd been tricked by a fox.
I don't think it was one.”
Going up the stairs to the first floor, we found that night had completely given way to dawn, and bright morning sun was pouring into the lounge.{g}
We squinted, gazing at the scene forever.
I put my hand on the lid and lifted it with all my strength.
A shrill laugh echoed all around.
everything? Surely not even the save data...”
I could see through to the other side of {n2}!
{n2} was fading away like a ghost!
{n2} reached her hand out toward me.
I tried to grab it and noticed that my own hand was see-through too.
